title: Ex‑Canadian Soldier Shoots at Yom Kippur Synagogue, Injures Officer in Suspected Antisemitic Attack.
body:
A gunman identified as a former Canadian soldier opened fire outside a synagogue in the New York‑area during Yom Kippur services on Tuesday, wounding a police officer before being shot dead by responding officers. The incident, which left the sanctuary itself largely untouched, has been labeled a possible antisemitic attack and has reignited concerns about the safety of religious sites during high‑profile holidays.

The shooting took place just after sunset, as congregants gathered for the holiest day in the Jewish calendar. Witnesses described a lone figure emerging from a nearby parking lot, brandishing a shotgun and firing a volley of rounds toward the building’s façade. Bullets shattered several windows and struck a nearby residence, but none of the roughly two dozen worshippers inside were hit. A New York City police detective who was on duty at the scene was struck in the thigh by a stray bullet and required medical attention. Police units from the precinct and the NYPD Emergency Service Unit converged on the location within minutes, returning fire that killed the assailant on the spot.

Law‑enforcement officials confirmed that the suspect, whose identity has not yet been released, had previously served in the Canadian Armed Forces before moving to the United States. Preliminary investigations suggest the motive may be rooted in antisemitic hatred, though authorities have not ruled out other possibilities. The FBI’s Joint Terrorism Task Force has been called in to assist with the probe, and the incident is being examined under both criminal and hate‑crime statutes. The rapid response by officers, which prevented further casualties, underscores the heightened security protocols that have become standard at many houses of worship across the country.

The attack arrives at a time when the United States is grappling with a surge in hate‑based violence. According to the Anti‑Defamation League, antisemitic incidents rose sharply in 2023, with more than 2,300 reported cases—an increase of 140 percent over the previous year. Synagogues, in particular, have been frequent targets, prompting the Department of Homeland Security to issue new guidelines for security assessments, staff training, and coordination with local police. Community leaders have repeatedly called for stronger federal support, arguing that existing resources are insufficient to protect congregations during major holidays when attendance spikes.

Local officials expressed both relief that the tragedy was limited in scope and outrage at the perpetrator’s actions. New York Mayor Eric Adams condemned the “heinous act of hatred” and pledged to allocate additional funding for security upgrades at vulnerable sites. Rabbi Jonathan Stein of the affected congregation emphasized the resilience of the community, noting that while the physical damage was repaired quickly, the emotional scar will linger. “We gather to pray for peace, and we will continue to pray for peace, even as we stand vigilant,” he said in a statement released after the shooting.

The incident also raises questions about the vetting and monitoring of former military personnel who immigrate to the United States. While the suspect’s service record has not been disclosed, experts note that the transition from armed forces to civilian life can be fraught, especially for individuals who may harbor extremist ideologies. Advocacy groups are urging both the U.S. and Canadian governments to improve information sharing regarding individuals with combat training who may pose a domestic threat.

As investigations continue, authorities are urging anyone with information about the shooter’s background or possible accomplices to come forward. The incident serves as a stark reminder that even well‑secured religious institutions are vulnerable to sudden, violent assaults. In the wake of the attack, security experts predict a further tightening of protective measures at synagogues, mosques, churches and other places of worship, especially during high‑profile observances. The hope among community leaders is that heightened vigilance will deter future threats and allow faith communities to worship without fear.
